title: Paediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Emergency Stabilisation and Specialist Transfer

evidenceAudit.scope: Paediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Emergency Stabilisation and Specialist Transfer
findings: Built as an additive Disease Management version using the approved-topic structure.
Investigations are ordered from bedside/laboratory assessment to imaging and specialist tests.
The original outline remains current; this version is non-current and pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: Saudi paediatric DKA fluid calculator, potassium bags and cerebral-injury medicine doses were not opened.
Ages 16–18 require the locally designated paediatric versus adult pathway.

pathophysiology.summary: Insulin deficiency causes hyperglycaemia, ketone production and metabolic acidosis. Osmotic diuresis causes dehydration and total-body electrolyte loss. Cerebral injury is the feared complication; fluid, insulin and neurological monitoring follow a paediatric protocol.
keyMechanisms: Insulin deficiency causes hyperglycaemia, ketone production and metabolic acidosis.
Osmotic diuresis causes dehydration and total-body electrolyte loss.
Cerebral injury is the feared complication; fluid, insulin and neurological monitoring follow a paediatric protocol.

symptoms: Polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss, abdominal pain, vomiting, weakness or reduced consciousness.
physicalSigns: Dehydration, Kussmaul breathing, ketotic breath, tachycardia and altered mental state.
redFlags: Shock, pH below 7.1, severe dehydration, falling consciousness, headache, bradycardia, hypertension or abnormal respiration suggesting cerebral injury.
precipitants: New type 1 diabetes, missed insulin, infection or pump failure.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Shock/systemic illness requiring parallel sepsis treatment.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Stabilise and commence high-frequency monitoring with senior paediatric/endocrine input.
ruleIn.normalValue: Normal age-adjusted observations and mental state

clinicalManagement.title: Stabilise and call specialist
actions: Use paediatric ABCDE; treat shock with source-defined bolus and obtain senior paediatric/endocrine/critical-care help.
Record weight and use the BSPED calculator/pathway for all fluids.

clinicalManagement.title: Replace fluid and start insulin
actions: Replace deficit plus maintenance over the source-defined period; include prior boluses in the calculation.
Start fixed-rate IV insulin only after fluids have begun and according to the paediatric pathway; never give an insulin bolus.

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor for cerebral injury
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Hourly and more often if severe
actions: Track neurological state, glucose, ketones, sodium and potassium.
Treat suspected cerebral injury immediately using the BSPED hypertonic-saline/mannitol pathway; do not wait for imaging.

regimens.dose: 0.05 units/kg/hour; use 0.1 units/kg/hour only where the BSPED pathway indicates
regimens.duration: Until DKA resolution and safe transition to subcutaneous insulin under paediatric diabetes guidance
adjustments: Use 0.05 units/kg/hour in most children and the source-defined higher rate selectively.
Adjust only with senior paediatric diabetes advice; check local Saudi protocol and formulary.
monitoring: Hourly glucose and ketones; frequent electrolytes, venous gas, fluid balance and neurological observations.
contraindications: Do not give an IV insulin bolus.
Correct/urgently manage severe hypokalaemia with senior input before continuing insulin.

branches.label: Paediatric DKA after initial fluid
branches.entryCriteria: Child or young person managed by a paediatric team with confirmed DKA after initial fluid resuscitation.

medicationPlan.note: All fluid, potassium, glucose and cerebral-injury treatments must use the weight-based BSPED/local paediatric DKA calculator and be checked independently.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Glucose above 11 mmol/L, venous pH below 7.3 or bicarbonate below 15 mmol/L, and blood ketones above 3 mmol/L.
Venous pH below 7.1 or bicarbonate below 5 mmol/L; assume 10% dehydration in the BSPED pathway.

teaching.scope: Paediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Emergency Stabilisation and Specialist Transfer
learningObjectives: Recognise the emergency and relevant red flags.
Select the correct investigation and escalation pathway.
Use medicines only within the stated branch and local formulary.
pitfalls: Delaying specialist escalation while waiting for a non-essential test.
Using an unverified medicine dose or applying an adult pathway to a child.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval.
keyPoints: Shock, pH below 7.1, severe dehydration, falling consciousness, headache, bradycardia, hypertension or abnormal respiration suggesting cerebral injury.
